3. Workspace lifetime, strict warnings and installed-toolchain evidence

Appendix B governs the handler shape. Allocation is completed before the inner handled sequence, which contains only the Decide_Work call; the handler frees and bare-reraises, and the normal path frees before return (Appendix B:20-32,46-62). This appropriately addresses RM 11.6's permission to disrupt assignments within the handled sequence when a language-defined check fails. The owner store is outside that sequence and is not modified by the borrowed call. This is a sound language-level placement argument, not proof of the generated landing pad or resource recovery. The relevant primary standard is [Ada 2022 RM 11.6, paragraphs 5/5–6/5](https://www.adaic.org/resources/add_content/standards/22rm/html/RM-11-6.html); Appendix B:77 correctly adds inspection of the owner store and handler landing pad to P-W6.

| Exit | Design treatment as amended | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| X1 | Free_Work then return (Appendix B:61-62) | Normal ownership is explicitly ended. |
| X2 | Allocator failure propagates outside the inner handler, before an owned result is assigned (Appendix B:53,70-71) | Nothing owned by Work needs Free. The obsolete function-level-handler/null-Free account in D3:1354 is superseded. |
| X3 | Callee Pre/Post, ghost statements, invariants and lemmas propagate through the inner handler (D3:1355; Appendix B:55-59) | Cleanup covers the proposed dynamic call; contract-wrapper placement and temporary finalization still need generated/native evidence. |
| X4 | Saved Old_Work/Carry_In/Old bignum storage failures propagate through the same handler when represented by an Ada exception (D3:1356) | All saved-value placement, exception paths and temporary finalization remain P-W6/PO-N7. |
| X5 | Unchecked stack overflow/process death is a hard native failure, never a recovered success/refusal (D3:1357) | Process cleanup does not establish the original success obligation. No claim of universal signal-to-Storage_Error recovery is accepted. |
| X6 | Caller Post runs after the inner invocation has freed its Work (D3:1358) | The old invocation has no live workspace; any new invocation made by that Post needs its own lifetime proof. |
| X7 | Base64/Byte_At declarations precede allocation (D3:1359; Appendix B:41-43) | No new Work exists yet. Reachability/failure evidence must distinguish genuine pre-allocation failures from proved-unreachable RTE paths. |

P-W1 checks legality of the exact scalar-result, Global-null, local-owner pattern, including the bare re-raise; “non-allocating” here is not a claim that its body executes no allocator. P-W2 requires end-of-scope and both Free ownership/leak proofs. P-W3 requires zero new warnings. P-W4 probes calls through checked Posts. P-W5 covers flow/ineffective assignments. P-W6 covers native fault paths, wrappers, storage placement, generated owner store/landing pad and temporary finalization. P-W7 repeats the applicable battery for both fallbacks. P-W8 preserves the sole original Off boundary (D3:1383-1417; Appendix B:72-78). None has been run in this review.

P-W3's risk is correctly retained as real, not waived: installed ug__exceptions_rte/test.out:1-4 reports “warning: unreachable branch” for the shown Constraint_Error exceptional contract. That saved output is an example, not a candidate result or a proof that every handler will warn. Installed ug__access4/test.adb:3-13 shows pool-specific Free, while ug__storage_error/storage.adb:4-13 uses an Off body. The latter is ineligible as a new boundary here (D3:303-310,1374-1376; H/HANDOFF.md:161).

The installed gnat2why binary contains the exact diagnostics “a loop invariant in a list of statements with an exception handler” and “… with a finally section” (GP/libexec/spark/bin/gnat2why, read-only string matches at binary line 37840). They constrain the syntactic list containing the invariant. Moving all loops/invariants into separately declared procedures leaves no loop invariant in the inner handler/finally list (D3:1287-1289; Appendix B:68-69). This is a correct application of the finding. Diagnostic strings alone do not prove that the complete call/borrow/exception pattern is supported.

CL-2 uses a post-guard local array and ordinary frame unwinding, with Appendix B's E-4 supplying the explicit Start expression (D3:1421-1443; Appendix B:17). It has no inherent cap, public Pre, Ghost suppression or warning waiver, so it remains an eligible lead-owned design alternative. Exact primary/secondary-stack placement, recursive call depth, stack protection and headroom for every originally successful input remain OPEN. A stack failure cannot become an accepted refusal.

CL-3 is experimental, not standard Ada. The installed GN/share/info/gnat_rm.info:25940-25944 and :27013-27075 confirm activation by -gnatX0 or Extensions_Allowed(All_Extensions), unconditional cleanup, and the prohibition on outward returns from the finally part. As amended, allocation stays outside the inner finally-protected block too (Appendix B:78). No native-rule prohibition inherently excludes it. It is unavailable as a closure if installed SPARK rejects it, if it needs a strict-warning waiver, or if it suppresses checked code. Its broadened language mode needs the specified separate GPT-6.1 review (D3:1445-1454). No fallback is selected or accepted by this review.

F-B2/F-B3 remain incomplete, operator-owned API/ABI packages, not ready repairs: checked function versions still execute in contracts, and scratch ABI custody/bounds/caller migration must preserve every capability (D3:1456-1461). Required change V3-RC2 repairs the control map's overstatement about X6/X7, and V3-RC3 repairs the mixed primary/staged invocation plan.
